question: A 3-month-old infant is clinically suspected to have DDH. Which imaging modality is most appropriate as the first-line investigation at this age?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Below 6 months the femoral head is largely cartilaginous and not visible on plain X-ray. Key bony landmarks (acetabular index, Hilgenreiner's line) are unreliable at this age.

Correct. Ultrasound is the gold-standard investigation for DDH in infants under 6 months. It directly visualises the cartilaginous femoral head and acetabular morphology, allowing dynamic assessment of hip stability.

Incorrect. MRI provides excellent soft-tissue detail but requires sedation in infants, is expensive, and is NOT the first-line modality. It is reserved for pre-operative planning in complex or older cases.
Incorrect. CT delivers significant radiation dose and is rarely indicated in the primary work-up of DDH. It may be used post-operatively to assess reduction but is not first-line in a 3-month-old.

overallFeedback.feedback: The femoral head is largely cartilage before ~4–6 months, making plain X-ray unreliable. Ultrasound (Graf classification) is the investigation of choice in this age group.
Well done. Remember the age threshold: ultrasound for <6 months (cartilaginous femoral head not X-ray-visible), plain X-ray from ~4–6 months once ossification has begun.
